title: Design System: Express Photo and Gifts

blue.note: The binding brand value, supplied by the shop. Owns the header, the cover's bands and leaning edge, the catalogue and the footer whole. On white it is the ink, the focus ring and the caret. Takes white text. In the shop: the catalogue title band, the current rail entry, the pressed photo toggle, the board's see-all door and a budget door under the pointer.

gold.note: The shop's highlighter: the Shop now action, the marked line, band slashes, marks on blue, the footer's phone and links underline. Pairs with ink or brand blue, never takes white text, never a region's background. In the shop: the count in the storefront sign, the Special chip, breadcrumb slashes, door go discs, the size chart's picked outline and radio dot.

leather.note: Same value as brand blue, named for its role as a ground so a surface and an accent are not confused at call sites.

paper.note: The body ground and the reading surface for the categories and the gifting section.

print.note: Cards, the photographs' own backing, the dock's round mark, the skip link.

ink.note: Body text on white, and the label on amber. The brand blue itself, 10.6:1 on white. There is no black.

ink-soft.note: Secondary prose on white: the blue let through to the white under it, 6.6:1.

on-leather-soft.note: Ledes, nav links and hours values on blue, 7.2:1.

rule-card.note: The 1px edge of every white door card.

rule-hair.note: The edge of every pill control on white: category and rail pills, the photo toggle, the selects.

rule-dark.note: The stronger line on blue: the size chart's outlines at rest and its radio rings.

display.purpose: The cover headline only, on its own leaning blue band.

band-strip.purpose: The words travelling on the strips between the wall's rows.

statement-loud.purpose: The gifting section's marked line, under a title already at display scale.

ledger-name.purpose: The row heading in the delivery/collection ledger.

subtitle.purpose: The catalogue's amber subtitle and the way headings.

card-title.purpose: Catalogue frame captions and product card names.

price.purpose: Prices on product cards and in the size chart, tabular; also the weight of pill labels and the Special chip.

cover-lede.purpose: The one sentence on the cover's slim band, 44ch.

address.purpose: The street address block in the footer.

body.purpose: Footer contact links and hours day labels. Below the 16px Floor: outstanding debt.

body-sm.purpose: The sign-up's explanatory line. Below the 16px Floor: outstanding debt.

micro.purpose: The desktop-only header nav and compact gold action.

mark.purpose: The footer's block headings, mono, tracked and uppercase, in amber on blue. Below the 16px Floor: outstanding debt.

count.purpose: Mono product counts on category and rail pills, and the size chart's measures. 16px: the one mono role that meets the floor.

shadows.name: shadow-gold
shadows.purpose: Under the amber action. Hover: 0 22px 44px -20px rgb(255 183 42 / 1).

shadows.name: shadow-blue
shadows.purpose: Under the blue button, the dock's round mark, a category tile in its blue state and the board's see-all door; its hover value under a budget door turned blue. Hover: 0 24px 48px -22px rgb(1 38 186 / 0.95).

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: The category tile, the catalogue frame, the product card, the budget door at rest and standalone photographs (cover wall prints, the storefront portrait). Hover: 0 30px 54px -30px rgb(1 38 186 / 0.5).

shadows.name: sign-lift
shadows.purpose: A filter under every leaning sign: the cover's, the gifting section's and the storefront's.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: State transitions: button lift, card raise, glow.

motion.name: expo.out
motion.purpose: Entrances: the signs running in along their lean (1.3s) and the reveal batch (0.9s).

motion.name: row-loops
motion.purpose: The cover wall's rows; the word strips run 66s / 52s so the wall never beats in time.

motion.name: wheel-scrub
motion.purpose: The catalogue wheel, geared to the page's scroll and bounded.

motion.name: wheel-hand
motion.purpose: Hand-turning the wheel: a touch swipe or the desktop arrows, written to --drag.

motion.name: shop-hover
motion.purpose: The shop's only motion: card and door lifts (4px), the blue turn, the go disc's -4deg tilt, the card photo's 1.04 scale. No scroll motion or entrances in the shop; recorded as headroom.

breakpoints.name: dock
breakpoints.note: Also: the dock's larger sizes, catalogue grid three-up, board three-up, glyphs and chart labels return.

breakpoints.name: shell
breakpoints.note: Also: the catalogue rail becomes a list beside the grid, shelves go four-up, the board six-up.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.note: The wheel's widest tuning and the catalogue grid four-up.

narrative.overview:
This is a printed shop, not an app. The argument is the shop's own work: the first thing a visitor meets is a full-bleed wall of real product photographs travelling past, with one plain sentence set on the widest of the wall's own blue bands, holding still while everything around it moves. From there the page reads the way the counter reads — one catalogue wheel turning with the scroll, eight category tiles that are each a door into the shop, then where to find the real door. One brand blue owns the loud surfaces whole — the header, the cover's bands, the catalogue and the footer — and white owns the rest: the wall's ground, the categories and the gifting promise, which carries its headline on one more leaning blue band. The page opens and closes on the same blue. Nothing is quiet for the sake of being quiet.

The shop under `/shop` is the same counter set for scanning. The storefront opens on the homepage's leaning sign, then lays one customer photograph beside every object it can go on; the catalogue carries the header's blue into a title band and puts the products on white beside a rail of categories. Every product is a white door with its price; every filter is a pill.

The density is deliberate and left-weighted: display type sits low-left at large clamped sizes with tight negative tracking, headings and actions hold one left edge from header to footer while the loud rows run full bleed past both, and long prose is capped at a 62ch measure so a wide shell never turns into a wide paragraph. Depth is low and warm — pill actions carry a coloured glow rather than a grey drop shadow, cards carry one soft blue-tinted lift, and everything else earns separation from its ground instead of from a shadow.

The system has one accent and uses it like a highlighter, not like a second brand colour. Amber marks the action to take and the line worth remembering; it never becomes a region. The client's rule is three colours in three roles: blue primary, white secondary, amber accent. There is no dark variant — `color-scheme: light` is declared, and the dark surfaces are compositional grounds, not a theme. The confirmed rejection is the previous build's sparse gallery treatment: the failure there was under-spending the material, not choosing the wrong material.
keyCharacteristics: Grounds in rotation: brand blue (loud), white and blue-white (reading), deep navy (the footer's close).
Amber as the accent only — actions, one marked line, band slashes, marks on dark. Never a region.
No black and no grey: every ink is the brand blue taken toward night.
Two families, strictly divided: Archivo for prose, Geist Mono for marks and measurements only.
Pill actions (999px), 12/18/22px surface radii, one soft blue-tinted elevation.
A white-ground photo wall whose headline is one of its own leaning blue bands, settling at its foot onto the catalogue's leaning edge.
Focus rings that change colour with their ground.
Motion animates from an already-visible default; with JS off the page is complete and merely still.
In the shop: one leaning sign, white product doors with prices, pills for every filter, mono for every count.

rules.name: The Highlighter Rule
rules.body: Amber marks; it does not upholster. It may carry a button, a line of text, a slash, a mark, a chip, an underline or a marker glyph. Nothing may be amber larger than the gifting section's highlighted line. An amber ground was tried for the gifting section and rejected by the client: it read as a warning sign and fought the blue.

rules.name: The Whole-Ground Rule
rules.body: A ground owns its section edge to edge. Blue, white, blue-white and night blue alternate as full-bleed bands; a coloured panel floating inside a differently-coloured section is not part of this world.

rules.name: The Three-Value Rule
rules.body: Only `#0126BA`, `#FFB72A` and `#FFFFFF` appear. Ink is the brand blue itself; softer text is that blue at 80% or 72% over white, or white at 80% over blue. There is no grey, no black, no navy and no tinted off-white.

rules.name: The 16px Floor
rules.body: No text element may be smaller than 16px on mobile, and no input, textarea or select may be, or mobile Safari zooms in on tap. This is the project owner's standing rule (CLAUDE.md), and it outranks the ramp above. **The shop meets it:** every text element under `/shop` is 16px or more at every width, the selects included, and inside `.shop` the site button is raised from 0.95rem to 1rem. Where a label could only fit by shrinking, it steps out instead — the "Takes your photo" glyph and the size chart's drawn label both hide under 46rem. **The shared footer and header do not yet meet it.** These roles are below 16px and are outstanding debt, not precedent: Body (15.5px), Body Small (14.5px), Mark (11.5px), Slot (12.5px), Measure (13.5px), Colophon (13px), and Micro (13.5px), which is desktop-only and so already clear of phones. Do not add a new text role below 16px, and raise these to 16px when the footer is next touched.

rules.name: The Two-Families Rule
rules.body: Archivo sets everything written in prose. Geist Mono sets only marks and measurements — the footer's block headings, the hours values, the colophon, the shop's product counts and the size chart's measures. Mono is never body copy, never a heading, never a button. Audit test: read the mono string aloud; if it is a sentence, it is in the wrong family.

rules.name: The Tight-Display Rule
rules.body: The larger the type, the tighter it sets: −0.035em and 0.94 line-height at display, −0.03em at headline, normal tracking by the time it is prose. Never letterspace Archivo positively; positive tracking (0.16em) belongs to mono alone.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose is capped — 62ch for ledes, 44ch on the cover, 44ch for fulfilment paragraphs, 36ch in the footer — regardless of how wide the 1400px shell gets.

rules.name: The One-Edge Rule
rules.body: Every band re-applies the shell and gutter. A full-bleed background never means full-bleed content.

rules.name: The Coloured-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is tinted by the thing casting it — amber under the amber button, brand blue under the blue button and the white card. Black or neutral-grey shadows are not part of this world.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: A list, a ledger or a table is separated by 1px hairlines, not by a border around each item: the gifting ledger, the hours table and the footer columns are all ruled. A card is not a list item — it is bordered when it is a *door*, something that can be pressed and that leads somewhere. The white doors are the category tile, the catalogue frame, the product card and the budget door; all wear the same 1px `{colors.rule-card}` edge and the same blue lift. The board's "see all" is a door filled blue instead, so it needs no edge. What does not go anywhere wears no edge: the customer portrait on the board is the visitor's picture, not a door, so it is a bare print with its corner and lift; the prints note is prose set off by one hairline, not a box. Audit test: if a bordered box does not go anywhere when you press it, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Two-Shape Rule
rules.body: Pill or soft rectangle. A square corner, a half-round "squircle" or a radius outside 12/18/22/999 is outside the system.

rules.name: The Wall's-Own-Devices Rule
rules.body: Every element of the cover is something the wall already has: prints, blue bands, the lean. Nothing is laid over the photographs: no plate, no scrim, no gradient, no shape that is not a band. A white plate, a foot fade, a side scrim, a 35mm film frame and a halftone dome rising from the catalogue were all tried and rejected; the dome covered two-thirds of the wall. If the headline grows, the rows shrink by the `svh` term before the sign may cover a row.

rules.name: The Icon Rule
rules.body: Category glyphs are drawn in `app/site/icons.tsx` on the shared 24px grid at the 1.6 stroke, as the object on the counter (two prints, a mitred frame, a photo mug, a cell, a ring, a camera, a wrapped box, a price tag). A new category gets a new drawing in the same hand, never a library icon.

rules.name: The Geared-Not-Driven Rule
rules.body: The wheel has no motion of its own. The page turns it by scrubbing it to the section's pass through the viewport — scrolling down turns it left, scrolling up turns it back — bounded at ±2.2 steps — and it stops the instant the visitor stops. The visitor can also turn it by hand, on a phone with a swipe that ignores mouse pointers and coasts a little on release, and on a wide screen with two arrow buttons that move it one whole frame at a time. The arrows are drawn `hidden` and only the script reveals them, because without it they would do nothing, and they are not drawn at all below 48rem. Nothing on this page autoplays below the cover.

rules.name: The From-Visible Rule
rules.body: Every tween is a `gsap.from` off an already-visible default. The markup renders complete; if the script never runs the page is intact and merely still. Nothing may be hidden in CSS and revealed by JS.

rules.name: The Single-Orchestrator Rule
rules.body: New motion goes into the existing `matchMedia` block, not into a new component effect. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` returns before a single tween is created — not after, and not by reverting them — and the global stylesheet additionally collapses every CSS keyframe animation to 0.001ms and cancels the hover transforms. **Reduced motion removes movement, not feedback:** colour, border and shadow transitions keep their authored duration, because the category tile turning blue and the sign-up's rule going amber are state, not animation.

dos: **Do** let a ground own its section edge to edge — brand blue (header, the cover's bands, catalogue, footer) alternating with white (the wall's ground, categories, gifting).
**Do** spend amber on the action, the marked line, the band slashes, marks on dark, `::marker` and `::selection` — and stop there.
**Do** set every mark, hours value, colophon and base line in Geist Mono, and everything readable as a sentence in Archivo.
**Do** keep the cover wall unwashed and set its type only on its own blue bands. Never lay a plate, scrim or shape over the photographs.

**Do** tune the focus ring to its ground: brand blue by default, amber inside `.on-dark`, ink on `.on-gold`. A single ring colour is invisible on one ground or the other — blue disappears into the blue panels, amber disappears into paper.
**Do** tint secondary text from its ground's hue (brand blue at 80% / 72% on white, white at 80% on blue).
**Do** rule lists and tables with hairlines, and reserve borders for the door cards that lead somewhere (category tile, catalogue frame, product card, budget door).
**Do** keep the category tiles four-by-two on a wide screen and two-by-four on a phone, names only.
**Do** gear the catalogue wheel to the visitor's own scroll rather than to a clock, and keep its turn inside the bound that holds the arc full.
**Do** animate from an already-visible default, inside the one `matchMedia` block.
**Do** cap prose at its measure (62ch default) no matter how wide the shell is.
**Do** keep every new text element at 16px or more on mobile, and every input, textarea and select too (The 16px Floor).
**Do** render product photographs with `ProductImage` at the widths it already offers (400 and 640), and let a new width join that list rather than appear at a call site.
**Do** make a second action on a section an amber-underlined `.inline-link` rather than a second button.
**Do** draw icons on the 24px grid at 1.6 stroke with round caps, and keep brand marks solid.
**Do** make every shop filter a 44px pill at 16px, current or pressed in whole brand blue, and set its counts in mono.
**Do** mark a picked state on blue with the amber edge alone, as the size chart does.
donts: **Don't** make amber the background of a region, section, card or hero. It is a highlighter, not an upholstery.
**Don't** set body copy, headings or button labels in mono, and don't letterspace Archivo positively.
**Don't** introduce a radius outside 12 / 18 / 22 / 999px, or square off a corner.
**Don't** use grey or black shadows; shadows are tinted by what casts them, and only actions, the door cards, the signs and standalone photographs cast one.
**Don't** float a coloured panel inside a differently-coloured section instead of banding the ground.
**Don't** use a grey neutral for secondary text.
**Don't** hide content in CSS for a JS reveal to uncover, and don't make a display row the only way to reach what it displays — the catalogue wheel shows a middle, and the link above it is the path.
**Don't** ship a dark-mode variant; `color-scheme: light` is declared and the dark grounds are composition, not theme.
**Don't** add a menu drawer or hamburger to the header; the bar is the wordmark and its icon controls on a phone, and the section links are a scroll away.
**Don't** put a product photograph in `public/` or ask Cloudinary for a size outside the shared list; the free plan meters every derived size and every byte stored.

**Don't** state a price that is not read from the catalogue, and don't add a review, a rating or a turnaround promise; none has been supplied (see `app/site/data.ts`). Shop prices come from Firestore only.
**Don't** swap Archivo for the template's Outfit or any other default face without a reason no other face could satisfy.
